analysis.title: Europe Open - Hold that thought
key_insights: US 10-year Treasury yield is sticky at 4.99% after US bond markets reopened and drifted. Tokyo desk saw decent buying in intermediates and some interest in rolling over in the 2-year zone.

USD rallied to May 2025 highs on Wednesday, but Citi traders were skeptical because volumes were much weaker on Veterans Day. EURUSD broke below 1.11 and USDJPY is just under 160 (overnight high 159.88).

Citi thinks actual yen intervention remains slim at current levels. JPY is considerably stronger on a trade-weighted basis, which limits the chance of intervention. Japan's Mimura said currency moves over the past few days have been too fast.
BoJ dove Asada said the bank is not taking a stance against raising rates no matter what, but must be careful about the pace of hikes. He would not propose a rate cut.

US PPI is due at 13:30 GMT. Citi economists expect final demand +0.3% MoM (vs 1.3% prior) and ex food, energy and trade +0.3% MoM (vs 0.5% prior). Core PCE is tracking at 0.33% MoM, and Citi is watching airfares, medical services and portfolio fees in the PPI details.
Fedspeak today: Hammack and Barr (both December voters), Goolsbee, Daly and Schmid. A 30-year Treasury auction is also due.
Taiex fell 2.6% on China President Xi's reunification comments and ongoing Nvidia weakness. Nasdaq futures are down 1.1% overnight and S&P e-minis are down 0.5%.

Citi Research says a leadership transition creates an overhang on Nvidia given the CEO's central role in strategy, product vision, customer relationships and investor confidence. Citi believes CFO Colette Kress could serve as interim CEO while the board evaluates external candidates.

Citi futures desk: S&P 7600 holds as support, and a break suggests a move to 7568. The CTA model flips long SPX above 7676, with max long at 7738. CTAs are long SX5E, with the level to return to short at 6313.

Brent is near $92 and roughly flat after bottoming. Iran's lead negotiator Ghalibaf said the US has not formally responded to Iran's letter. Witkoff and Kushner meet Putin in Moscow today after US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, where territorial issues remain a sticking point. Gold broke through $4000 overnight.
UK Q3 GDP printed +0.7% QoQ and +1.9% YoY. Citi says resilient growth supports another BoE hike, with February more likely than December, dependent on energy prices.
Romania Oct CPI printed 6.94% YoY vs 6.61% prior, slightly above consensus. The NBR should hold the policy rate.

Brazil's government unveiled fiscal tightening measures worth BRL 50-60bn that cap real spending growth at 2% from 2027 (down from 2.5%). Brazil IPCA and Argentina CPI are due today, and Peru's central bank is expected to hold.

Citi's CTA model flips long SPX above 7676, with max long at 7738. First buy levels in NDX and RTY are 29798 and 2891. CTAs are long SX5E, with the level to return to short at 6313.
geopolitical: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner are meeting Russian President Putin in Moscow today after US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, where territorial issues remain a sticking point.
US-Iran talks are at a standstill. Iran's lead negotiator Ghalibaf said the US has not formally responded to Iran's letter.
China President Xi said China's reunification must and will be achieved, which weighed on Taiwan's Taiex.
Indonesia VP Gibran formally submitted his resignation. The assembly will elect a successor within 60 days from two candidates President Prabowo plans to nominate.
